A1.justification: Both PDFs contain the same research work and readable material across 32 pages, including Appendices A-E. Pages 2-32 are identical in extracted text and rendered appearance; the first-page scientific text is also unchanged.

before.justification: v1 reports original simulation, ablation, robustness and real-robot results in Sections 4-5 and Appendices B-D, including Meta-World/LIBERO evaluations and 25 real-world towel-sorting trials.

after.justification: v2 retains the original simulation and real-robot results in Sections 4-5 and Appendices B-D. These include benchmark success rates, ablations and the towel-sorting evaluation.

M1.justification: Section 3 retains the same VQ-VAE tokenizer, masked transformer, training losses, MGP-Short sampling and MGP-Long adaptive token refinement. No model component or procedure changes.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same Meta-World and LIBERO tasks, missing-observation and dynamic scenarios, non-Markovian button tasks, Push-T multimodality analysis and real-world towel-sorting task.

E2.justification: Corresponding comparisons retain identical baseline membership, including DP/DP3, Consistency Policy, FlowPolicy, QueST and the other autoregressive baselines. The DP3-Full Seq. real-world comparison is also unchanged.

E3.justification: Demonstration counts, rollout counts, checkpoint selection, success and latency metrics, preprocessing, and training/inference settings are identical in Sections 4-5 and Appendix A.

E4.justification: The seven ablations in Appendix B, robustness tests, confidence-score analyses, tokenization accuracy and multimodality analyses in Appendix C, and real-world failure/input analyses in Appendix D are unchanged.

E5.justification: Both versions report the same three-seed Meta-World evaluation and aggregation procedure in Section 4.1. No repeated-run information, uncertainty estimates or statistical testing procedures are added or revised.

E6.justification: All numerical and qualitative results, including appendix entries, are unchanged. Table 3 retains 0.889 for MGP-Short on LIBERO-90 and 0.820 for MGP-Long on LIBERO-Long; Section 5 retains 96% versus 84% real-world success.

T1.justification: The mathematical definitions, assumptions and Equations (1)-(6) are identical. No formal result, proof or derivation is added, removed or revised.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction contributions and conclusion retain identical claims about MGP's novelty, inference efficiency, success rates and robustness on long-horizon and non-Markovian tasks.

C2.justification: Interpretations of confidence-guided refinement and failure cases remain unchanged, as do the two-stage training mismatch and complexity limitation in Section 6 and applicability discussions in Appendices C-D.

D1.justification: Appendix A's hyperparameters and data-processing details, Appendix C.6's model size and timing information, and Appendix D.1's real-robot implementation details are identical. Resource-access information is also unchanged.

R1.justification: Section 2 and the reference list are identical. Positioning relative to diffusion policies, autoregressive policies and earlier masked generative models is unchanged.

P1.justification: v2 adds Edmond S. L. Ho to the author list and updates the arXiv version/date stamp from 9 December 2025 to 26 January 2026. Scientific prose, headings and section ordering are unchanged.

P2.justification: The first-page author block is slightly repositioned to accommodate the additional author, and the margin stamp changes. All figures, tables, captions and subsequent page layouts are identical.

improvement.justification: The revision changes authorship and first-page metadata/layout only. Scientific exposition, methods, empirical evidence, reproducibility information and limitations remain identical throughout the main text and appendices, establishing no meaningful net difference in overall paper quality.
